( 4) At any time before or within 6 months after the date directed for the taking of the census, if instructed by any Assistant Superintendent so to do, any census officer may visit any dwelling-house within the area for which he is appointed for the purpose of checking any information or of obtaining further information for the purof the census, in which event, after exercising the powers conferred upon him by section 8, he shall(a) if satisfied that a schedule relating to any dwelling-house contains the name of any person who was not within that dwelling-house at the time of the taking of the census, delete from such schedule the name of, and all particulars relating to, the said person; and

(b) if satisfied that any person was within any dwelling-house at the time of the taking of the census whose name is not written in a schedule to that dwelling-house, enter the name of, and all particulars relating to, the said person in or in a separate schedule, as the Superintendent may direct; and

(c) if satisfied that any schedule is incorrect in any other material particular make any necessary correction thereto.

Any census officer and any person employed in the Offences by of the abstract required to be made under the il~R~~~s last preceding section who

(a) without sufficient cause, refuse or neglects to comply with any instruction or requisition to him by the Superintendent or an Assistant Superintendent, or fails to use reasonable diligence in performing any duty imposed on him; or

(b) wilfully puts an offensive or improper question; or

(c) knowingly makes any false return; or

(d) asks, receives, or takes from any person than an authorised officer of the Government any payment or reward; or

(e) save in the public interest and with the perof the Superintendent discloses any information which has come to his knowledge in the of his duty as such; of an offence: Penalty, a fine of $2,500 and imprisonment for 6 months.

(1) Any person who(a) refuses to answer truthfully, to the best of and belief, any question asked of him by a census officer which he is legally bound so to answer or wilfully makes a false answer thereto; or B.L.R.O. l/J984

(b) makes, signs, delivers or causes to be made, or delivered any wilfully false or incorrect statement, or return; or

(c) refuses to allow a census officer such reasonable access to any land, house, enclosure, vessel or place as he is required by this Act to allow; - or

(d) removes, obliterates, alters or injures, before the expiry of 6 months from the time of taking the census, any letters, marks or numbers which have been painted, marked or affixed for the purof the census; or

(e) refuses or neglects to comply with any provision of this Act or of any rule made thereunder; of an offence: Penalty, a fine of $2,500 and imprisonment for 6 months.

(2) Any person who impersonates a census officer of an offence: Penalty, a fine of $5,000 and imprisonment for 12 months.
No prosecution shall be instituted under this Act without the previous sanction in writing of the Attorney

No entry in any book, register, or record made by a or by any other person in the discharge of his in duty under this Act shall be admissible as evidence in any or criminal proceeding, save and except a prosecution under this Act in respect of such entry against the person who made, signed or delivered the same, or caused the same to be made, signed or delivered.
